carnage.name: MashedBROtato
carnage.commentary: That’s not a missed green; that’s a prolonged emergency in the pinestraw. Once the ball started ricocheting between sand, rough, and more sand, this hole turned into a hostage situation and demanded every stupid recovery shot on the property.

carnage.name: Leroy4522
carnage.commentary: A par 5 that somehow required a small tax return of extra swings. The damage was less one giant blowup than a steady stream of “surely the next one gets us out of here,” which is how a hole quietly eats you alive.

carnage.name: derekldavis
carnage.commentary: This one was pure contact-hell: rough, more rough, sand, more sand, then finally a mercy finish from short range. When the middle of the hole becomes a recycle bin, the scorecard usually stops being polite about it.

carnage.name: IUDoc92
carnage.commentary: That hole was a full-on short-game mutiny. The tee shot and approach didn’t save him, but the real damage was the endless little misses around the green that kept turning a bad spot into a bigger damn mess.

players.name: IUDoc92
players.tagline: The approach game showed up; the short game filed for unemployment.
players.body: This was a familiar IUDoc92 special: enough good iron play to keep the scoreboard from completely melting, then a short-game collapse to drag the whole thing under. The approach work was the best part of the bag, but the benchmark-ugly short game and a couple of extra putts turned decent positioning into a pile of bogeys and doubles. The worst hole was textbook damage control gone wrong, and the 18th at least showed he can still cash one in when the bumpy stuff behaves. Across a strong run of prior starts, this is still basically the same story: some useful tee-to-green flashes, but not nearly enough cleanup around the greens to protect the round.

players.name: derekldavis
players.tagline: A tee game so crooked it needed its own warning label.
players.body: derekldavis brought a full demolition project off the tee and then kept the wreckage rolling all the way to the hole. The irons and putter never really got a clean chance because the round was already bleeding from the first swing, and zero greens in regulation tells the whole ugly story without needing a lawyer. The 13th was the perfect postcard: sand, more sand, more sand, then a late mercy finish from close range after the hole had already eaten him alive. After one prior look, this wasn’t a trend so much as a louder version of the same nasty shape, just with even less recovery and way more noise.

players.name: Leroy4522
players.tagline: The putter was basically on a smoke break while the rest of it burned.
players.body: Leroy4522 didn’t get buried by one disaster; he got chewed up by a bunch of medium-sized ones, which is somehow worse. The ball-striking was fine enough to keep him around the property, but the putter was cold, the three-putts piled up, and the round never found a gear that looked even remotely sustainable. The 13th was the poster child: plenty of movement, a weird patch of concrete in the middle of the chaos, and then a finish that said the hole was in charge the whole time. With ten prior starts, the profile is getting pretty clear: there’s enough occasional tee-and-approach pop to stay dangerous, but the cleanup work is too volatile to trust for long.

players.name: MashedBROtato
players.tagline: He found every bad lie in the zip code and collected them like souvenirs.
players.body: MashedBROtato had the biggest raw heat on the card and still spent most of the round punching out of bad neighborhoods like the course owed him money. The driver showed up in flashes, but the approach game and short-game mess kept turning opportunities into survival drills, and the putter never arrived with a rescue plan. The 11th was the ugliest of the uglies: a full-blown pinestraw/sand pinball machine that kept resetting the ball farther from salvation until the hole finally stopped laughing. That said, the 5th and 13th prove there’s still enough juice to make birdie looks and the occasional clean hole; the problem is the round has to survive long enough to use them.
